title: Dilemma
description: One Would You Rather choice in the bank, written as a spoken stem plus two short fragments. The screen only ever shows the fragments; the stem is what the voiceover says to make them a question. Scores are assigned at harvest; measured_split is filled in only after a real Community poll closes.

id.description: Stable id, e.g. d0042. Never reused, even after the dilemma is used.

stem.description: The shared setup, spoken and never rendered: 'Would you rather never feel'. Together with the two fragments it has to read as one natural sentence.

option_a.description: Top field, always #FF1E1E. 22 is the hard cap (two lines of Nunito 900 at 96px); 16 or under lands on one line and is the target. Lowercase, no trailing punctuation, never contains 'or'.

option_b.description: Bottom field, always #0A84FF. Same constraints as option_a. The pair usually ends on the same word — the repetition is what makes them scan as a single choice.

image_a.description: Path to the cut-out subject for the top field: no photographic background, subject in the upper half of the frame. Required before the dilemma can ship, though the composition still renders without it.

image_b.description: Path to the cut-out subject for the bottom field. Same treatment as image_a.

vertical.description: Food is the entry wedge: it carries breakout videos at every channel size and dominates the audience's own vocabulary.

scores.description: Each 1-5. Rank is the product. A zero on any axis means discard, not fix.

polarization.description: Will the split land between 55/45 and 88/12?

universality.description: Applies to everyone watching, with no precondition to own or be something.

instant_read.description: Both fragments understood in under two seconds. One line each scores highest.

imageable.description: Each fragment names one thing that can be photographed as a cut-out subject. This replaced the old 'renders as text alone' axis: the format is image-led, and a fragment with nothing to picture cannot carry a field.

counterintuitive.description: Marks a dilemma where the expected majority is wrong. Every episode needs at least one — this is the block that produces the comments.

already_am_that.description: Names a condition many viewers already live with. Reliably produces self-deprecating replies ('I already have bad eyesight lol', 49 likes).

difficulty.description: Position in the episode's ramp. Each episode uses one of each, in this order.

source.description: Where it came from, so the harvest can be evaluated by yield.

ref.description: Video id, report path, or free text.

status.description: banked -> scheduled into an episode -> polled on the Community tab -> used in a published episode.

measured_split.description: Real Community-poll result. Absent until the poll closes; never estimated, never invented.
